questions.question: What is the primary goal of a linear search algorithm?
questions.gold_answer: The primary goal of a linear search is to find a specific key within an array and return its index. If the key is not found, the algorithm returns -1.
questions.quote: Is key ko humein find karna hai apne array mein aur woh jis bhi index pe present hai array mein, woh index humein return karna hoga. And if that key is not present in that array, toh we will return -1.
questions.question_hi: linear search algorithm ka main goal kya hota hai?

questions.question: What is the time complexity of a linear search?
questions.gold_answer: The time complexity of a linear search is O(n), because in the worst case, you have to traverse every element in an array of size n.
questions.quote: Kyunki n size ka agar array hai, toh hum poore array ko traverse kar rahe hain, toh uski jo time complexity ho jaayegi, woh ho jaayegi O(n).
questions.question_hi: linear search ka time complexity kya hai?

questions.question: What is the main requirement for an array to be used with binary search?
questions.gold_answer: For binary search to work, the elements in the array must be in a sorted order, typically increasing order.
questions.quote: Toh binary search implement karne ke liye humare jo elements hain array mein, woh sorted order mein present hone chahiye.
questions.question_hi: binary search ke liye array mein kya condition honi chahiye?

questions.question: What is the time complexity of binary search?
questions.gold_answer: The time complexity of binary search is O(log n base 2), which makes it more efficient than linear search.
questions.quote: Toh humara jo complexity hai, woh ho jaayega O(log n base 2).
questions.question_hi: binary search ka time complexity kya hota hai?

questions.question: In binary search, how do you determine if the target key is in the first or second half of the current range?
questions.gold_answer: You compare the key to the middle element. If the key is smaller than the middle element, it must be in the first half; if it is larger, it must be in the second half.
questions.quote: Toh hum 21 se compare karenge 27 ko ki kya woh usse kam hai ya zyada. Toh 27 jo hai yahan pe humare mid element se zyada hai. Toh ye toh pakka hai ki 27 isse pehle present nahi hoga.

questions.question: Why is binary search considered better than linear search?
questions.gold_answer: Binary search is considered better because it has a lower time complexity, O(log n), compared to linear search's O(n), meaning it takes less time to find an element.
questions.quote: Binary search is a better searching algorithm than linear search as it takes less time.

questions.question: What is the specific formula used to calculate the middle index in the binary search code?
questions.gold_answer: The middle index is calculated by adding the start and end pointers and dividing by two: (s + e) / 2.

dropped_unverified.question: How does binary search reduce the search space during each iteration?
dropped_unverified.gold_answer: Binary search compares the key with the middle element of the current range. Based on the comparison, it discards half of the remaining array, effectively halving the search space in each step.
dropped_unverified.quote: Toh humara jo searching part hai jahan pe humein search karna hai apni key ke liye, woh kam ho gaya. Pehle woh poora array tha aur ab woh aadha array ho gaya.

dropped_unverified.question: What happens to the pointers in binary search when the key is not found in the current half?
dropped_unverified.gold_answer: The start or end pointers are updated to narrow the search range. Specifically, the end pointer is set to mid-1 if the key is smaller, or the start pointer is set to mid+1 if the key is larger.
